pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: Office or home?
paragraphs: Fictional worker’s needs: quiet concentration, regular team contact, flexible hours. Home, office and hybrid each offer benefits and drawbacks. No one option is universally best. Recommend a routine only after checking how the needs fit together.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Do you work better at home or in an office?
lines.audioText: Do you work better at home or in an office?
lines.translation: Você trabalha melhor em casa ou no escritório?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: At home, usually, because I can concentrate without interruptions
lines.audioText: At home, usually, because I can concentrate without interruptions.
lines.translation: Em casa, geralmente, porque consigo me concentrar sem interrupções

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I understand that. However, I miss the quick conversations with the team
lines.audioText: I understand that. However, I miss the quick conversations with the team.
lines.translation: Entendo. Porém, sinto falta das conversas rápidas com a equipe

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Me too. Although I prefer home, I wouldn’t want to work alone all week
lines.audioText: Me too. Although I prefer home, I wouldn’t want to work alone all week.
lines.translation: Eu também. Embora prefira casa, não gostaria de trabalhar sozinha a semana toda

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Would a hybrid routine solve that?

lines.audioText: Good point. We could have two shared team days and keep the rest flexible.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That’s worth trying. Let’s check whether it gives us enough quiet time too
lines.audioText: That’s worth trying. Let’s check whether it gives us enough quiet time too.

pages.title: Recommend a working routine
pages.instruction: Recommend a routine and respond to my concern

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Hybrid works, but the schedule doesn’t. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. Working at home helps me concentrate, and two office days make it easier to speak to the team. However, the office days have been changing at short notice, so planning childcare and travel has become difficult. I don’t want to stop seeing colleagues. I’d like to keep the benefit but make the schedule more predictable. What would you suggest I ask the team to agree on? I don’t think one routine has to be best for everyone
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. Working at home helps me concentrate, and two office days make it easier to speak to the team. However, the office days have been changing at short notice, so planning childcare and travel has become difficult. I don’t want to stop seeing colleagues. I’d like to keep the benefit but make the schedule more predictable. What would you suggest I ask the team to agree on? I don’t think one routine has to be best for everyone.
pages.greeting: Hybrid working helps, but the schedule is a problem

items.prompt: Negotiate a work routine with one benefit and one drawback

items.answer: Example: Home is quieter, but I miss quick team discussions. How about two office days?
